name: Send certificate expiry alerts from Google Sheets via SMTP email
description:
## Quick overview
This workflow runs daily at 7am to read an expiry register from Google Sheets, categorize items by how soon they expire, and send escalating reminder emails via SMTP for already-expired items and upcoming renewals.

## How it works
1. Runs every day at 7am on a schedule.
2. Reads all rows from a Google Sheets compliance register that includes expiry dates.
3. Calculates days remaining for each item and groups them into expired, within 7 days, within 30 days, and within 90 days lists.
4. Stops without sending anything when there are no items due or expired.
5. Sends an urgent email when one or more items are already expired, optionally including items expiring within 7 days.
6. Sends a renewals summary email when there are no expired items, including the 90-day horizon list only on Mondays.

## Setup
1. Add Google Sheets credentials and select the target spreadsheet and sheet in the Google Sheets read step.
2. Ensure your sheet has the columns Item, Type, Holder, Expires, RenewalContact, and Notes (with Expires in a parseable date format).
3. Add SMTP/Email Send credentials and replace the recipient address (owner@example.com) in both email steps.
4. Adjust the 7am cron expression if you want the check to run at a different time.

## Requirements
- A Google account for the Sheets register; an SMTP or Gmail account for the alert emails; an n8n instance (cloud or self-hosted) that can run a daily schedule.

## Customization
- Change the 90/30/7-day escalation windows in the Code node; add SMS or Slack alongside the email alerts; track any dated item - insurance, licences, MOT, certifications, contracts - by adding rows to the same register.

## Additional info
The escalation logic is deliberately asymmetric: expired items alert every day, approaching deadlines only at 90, 30 and 7 days - so the alert inbox stays meaningful instead of training you to ignore it. Reminders are grouped into one digest email per run rather than one email per item. Built by Digital Dots (https://digitaldotsent.com), who build automation for small service businesses.

workflow.name: Track certificate and insurance expiry dates in Google Sheets and send escalating email reminders

parameters.content:
## Track certificate and insurance expiry dates in Google Sheets and send escalating email reminders

### How it works

1. A schedule trigger fires at 7am daily and reads the whole compliance register from Google Sheets.
2. A Code node compares every Expires date to today and sorts rows into expired, within-7-days, within-30-days and within-90-days buckets.
3. An IF gate ends the run silently on days when nothing is due, so the workflow never nags.
4. A second IF splits anything already expired away from merely upcoming renewals.
5. Expired items trigger an urgent "you may not be covered" email; upcoming ones get a calmer renewals summary, with the 90-day horizon list included only on Mondays.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Connect Google Sheets credentials and point "Get expiry register from Google Sheets" at your compliance sheet.
- [ ] Give the sheet the columns Item, Type, Holder, Expires, RenewalContact, Notes and enter every policy, certificate and registration once.
- [ ] Add SMTP credentials and replace owner@example.com in both email nodes.
- [ ] Adjust the 7am cron in "Run daily expiry check at 7am" to match your working day.

### Customization

Change the 7/30/90-day thresholds in "Sort items into expiry windows" to match your own renewal lead times, or add a Slack or SMS node next to "Send expired items alert email" for louder escalation.

---

Built by [Digital Dots](https://digitaldotsent.com)

## 1. Read the register daily

The **Run daily expiry check at 7am** schedule trigger fires every morning, then **Get expiry register from Google Sheets** pulls every certificate, policy and registration row - each with its expiry date - into the workflow.

## 2. Bucket by days remaining

The **Sort items into expiry windows** Code node compares each expiry date against today and groups every item into one of four buckets: already expired, within 7 days, within 30 days, or within 90 days.

## 3. Decide whether to email

**Continue only if something needs action** stays silent when nothing is due, so you get no empty emails. **Check for already expired items** then splits genuinely expired items away from the ones merely approaching their deadline.

## 4. Send the escalating alert

**Send expired items alert email** raises an urgent cover-lapse warning; **Send upcoming renewals email** sends a calmer heads-up for what is coming due. Two tones, so an expired certificate never reads like a routine reminder.
